topics.label: Course Overview and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, describes the student cohort, and sets out the learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Genetic and Developmental Basis of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the accumulation of genetic changes leads to cancer through the disruption of normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture, and consider the experimental approaches used to study it.

topics.label: Distinguishing Benign and Malignant Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biological criteria, progression pathways, and nomenclature used to differentiate benign neoplasms from invasive and metastatic malignancies.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physiological and mechanical processes through which localized and metastatic tumors cause systemic illness and death in patients.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence Across Humans and Other Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the comparative frequency and distribution of neoplastic diseases across human populations and other animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical Presentation and Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical signs of cancer and the rationale, efficacy, and limitations of population screening programs across various tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and practical session arrangements.
